consequence.statement: Environments using OperatorHub or Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM) to deploy or update cert-manager can no longer obtain versions beyond v1.16.5 from those sources; updates must switch to alternative distribution methods.
consequence.remediation: Switch to alternative cert-manager installation methods (Helm, direct manifests, or cloud-provider distributions) for versions after v1.16.5.

original.statement: cert-manager no longer publishes packages to OperatorHub, with v1.16.5 being the last release available on OperatorHub and the cert-manager-olm repository archived.

consequence.statement: No cert-manager releases after v1.16.5 are published to OperatorHub (RedHat OpenShift OperatorHub or operatorhub.io). Installs managed through OperatorHub/OLM stay on v1.16.5 and get no newer versions from that source. The evidence does not say that the existing install fails.
consequence.remediation: If you install cert-manager from OperatorHub/OLM and need versions after v1.16.5, plan to move to another distribution method. The cert-manager-olm repository is archived.

corrected.statement: cert-manager no longer publishes OperatorHub packages. v1.16.5 is the last release on RedHat OpenShift OperatorHub and operatorhub.io, and the cert-manager-olm repository is archived. Installs from OperatorHub keep working but get no newer versions from that channel.

decision.reason: [ev-c3d5e62490c3] says only that cert-manager no longer publishes OperatorHub packages, that v1.16.5 is the last release on OperatorHub and that the cert-manager-olm repository is archived. It does not say that any configured value stops being honoured, so setting-ignored is not supported. It also does not say that anything fails or that a migration is required. An OperatorHub-based install keeps running v1.16.5 and simply gets no newer packages from that channel. That is a review-level behavior-change, not mandatory work.
